title: basicly implementation-plan handoff artifact
description: What DECOMPOSE hands BUILD (factory loop requirements 8). One artifact per decompose event, recorded on the feature that was decomposed. It carries the six fields the plan gate already refuses a child for, resolved onto the ids the decomposition created, plus the graph those ids were grouped into - so BUILD reads the plan it is held to instead of re-deriving it from each child's body.

schema_version.description: Artifact-format version; bump only when a consumer's contract changes.

feature.description: The issue id that was decomposed into these tasks.

tasks.description: One entry per planned child, in the plan's declared order. A plan with no task is not a plan, which is the whole-plan rule plan_gate.gate_plan states first.

issue_id.description: The recorded child this planned task became.

title.description: The child's title, which the plan's declared graph is keyed on.

acceptance.description: Testable acceptance criteria. At least one, so VERIFY has a check to derive rather than a judgement to make.

scope.description: The file globs this task declares it touches, so parallel safety is computable and the landing scope check has something to hold the lane to.

depends_on.description: Sibling ids this task follows, declared and computed edges unioned. Empty is a declared answer; the key being absent is silence, which is why it is required.

budget_tokens.description: What this unit is worth spending. A budget that cannot be spent is not a budget.

integrity.description: The level selecting this unit's gate set, model tier and rework allowance.

demonstration.description: How this task is exercised end to end through the consumer surface (D18) - the command, request or test that demonstrates it. Required here, unlike in the build-entry predicate over a recorded bead: this artifact's only producer is a decomposition plan_gate.require_plan already passed, so there is no population whose silence could be mistaken for a defect. That it names something runnable is the gate's rule, not restated here, on the same grounds scope does not re-encode what makes a string a glob.

groups.description: The graph: ids per parallel group, in declared order. Distinct groups are safe to build concurrently; within a group the order is the serial build order.
